reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: All 3 gates passed: GET is an exported HTTP route handler (Gate 1 public-API exception); BUG_BOUNTY_SCOPE.json has no trust_assumptions and entry point is unauthenticated external HTTP (Gate 2 N/A); src/app/auth/ is explicitly in-scope (Gate 3 passes). Code confirms the violation: cookie deletion at L113-119 is guarded by `if (!error)` inside `if (code)`, so both the error-exchange path (L124) and no-code path (L128) return without deleting the httpOnly `oauth_redirect` cookie (sameSite=lax, maxAge=600). An attacker can trigger this via the Discord OAuth callback endpoint by (1) tricking the victim into initiating an OAuth flow for the attacker's registered client (setting `oauth_redirect` to the attacker's consent URL), then (2) inducing a failed callback via an invalid/replayed code within the 10-minute cookie window, causing the stale `oauth_redirect` cookie to persist and redirect the victim into the attacker's OAuth consent page on their next successful login — however, the multi-step timing requirement and prerequisite of a registered OAuth client make full exploitation uncertain.
